description: Every interactive element must have a visible or programmatic label for screen readers.
ImageButton and clickable ImageView must have a content description.
No two interactive elements should share identical text/content-desc unless same action.
Tappable elements must meet minimum size (48x48 dp).
Every EditText must have a programmatic label (hint, labelFor, or content-desc).
Critical controls must not be disabled without explanation or alternative.
Zero-area or invalid bounds must be removed from focus tree.
Elements must not overlap in ways that hide content or break focus order.
Text and UI components must meet minimum contrast ratios.
Text bounds must fit full content without clipping.
Color must not be the only indicator of state or meaning.
Video with spoken audio must provide captions/subtitles.
Audio-only content must have a text transcript in the UI.
Alerts must include visual indicators, not sound alone.
Focus order must follow natural top-to-bottom reading sequence.
Decorative elements must be excluded from accessibility focus.
Adjacent targets need >=8 dp spacing to prevent mis-taps.
All functionality must work with a single pointer.
Irreversible actions must require confirmation.
Labels must remain visible while typing.
Errors must identify the field and how to fix it.
Password fields should offer reveal/hide control.
Back, home, close, menu buttons must have descriptive labels.
Every screen needs a visible title or heading.
Animation/auto-update must be pausable/stoppable.
Timed sessions must warn >=20s before expiry with extend option.
Use plain, simple language in labels and hints.
Text must remain readable at 200% system font size.
All-caps must not be used for paragraph or instruction text.
Icon-only buttons must have content-desc describing the action.
